entities.name: Luke of Padua
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Luke of Padua (c. 1206–1286) was a religious figure associated with Padua in the thirteenth century, remembered in local Catholic tradition amid the city’s flourishing mendicant and civic saint culture—the age that also exalted Anthony of Padua. His profile fits the dense landscape of friars, hermits, and holy men who structured communal devotion in communal Italy.

Documentation is thinner than for Padua’s superstar saints, suggesting a locally commemorated holy life rather than a pan-European cult. Nonetheless such figures sustained neighbourhood piety, confraternities, and the religious identity of a university and market city on the Veneto plain.

Luke illustrates how medieval Italian cities stacked multiple sacred personae beside their principal patrons.
